directAnswer: Your computer may be running slowly due to insufficient RAM, background processes, or malware. Identifying and addressing these issues can significantly improve performance.
summary: Several factors can contribute to a slow computer, including hardware limitations, software issues, and external threats like malware.

sections.heading: Hardware Limitations
sections.body: Older computers may struggle with modern software demands. Upgrading RAM or switching to an SSD can provide noticeable performance improvements.

sections.heading: Software Issues
sections.body: Too many background applications can consume system resources. Regularly checking and managing startup programs can help free up resources.

sections.heading: Malware Threats
sections.body: Malware can significantly slow down your computer. Running a full system scan with a reputable antivirus program is essential.

steps.title: Check Task Manager (Windows)
steps.detail: Press Ctrl + Shift + Esc to open Task Manager. Look for processes using high CPU or memory and end unnecessary tasks.

steps.title: Manage Startup Programs (Windows)
steps.detail: In Task Manager, go to the Startup tab and disable programs that you do not need to launch at startup.

steps.title: Run Disk Cleanup (Windows)
steps.detail: Search for 'Disk Cleanup' in the Start menu, select the drive you want to clean, and follow the prompts to remove temporary files.

steps.title: Check for Malware (Mac)
steps.detail: Use a malware detection tool like Malwarebytes to scan your Mac for potential threats and remove them.

faqs.question: How can I tell if my computer has malware?
faqs.answer: Signs of malware include unexpected pop-ups, slow performance, and programs that start without your permission.

faqs.question: Will adding more RAM always improve performance?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. If your computer is already using sufficient RAM for your tasks, adding more may not yield significant improvements.

faqs.question: What if my computer is still slow after following these steps?
faqs.answer: Consider performing a system restore to a previous point, or consult a professional for hardware diagnostics.

caveats: Performance issues can vary greatly depending on the specific hardware and software configuration of your computer.
